LESSON: GALLOPING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.2: Galloping
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Galloping, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How does a horse gallop?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify different directions of galloping for agility and coordination,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Galloping in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform galloping in different directions for skill acquisition  Learners to observe video or demonstrations of galloping and talk about the body movement. Learners with postural defects or short stature could be appropriately positioned for comfort and clear view. Screen resolution and light intensity could be regulated for learners who are sensitive to light. How does a horse gallop? 24 circular and zigzag.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Galloping in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy playing galloping games while moving in different directions.  Learners to demonstrate galloping. Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding activity, or perform at their level of functional ability.  Learners to practise galloping in different directions. Safety of all learners should be observed and extra caution taken for learners with chronic health conditions.  Learners to practice galloping to make patterns. Organize a safe conducive environment.  Learners to play games while galloping in different directions and give self and other group members feedback. Learners with mobility difficulties and those on mobility devices could be supported. 25

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Galloping together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Self-efficacy: learners: as the learner focusses on practising galloping skills by accepting feedback from peers.

 Communication and collaboration: as the learner interacts with peers while playing games that involve galloping.

Values:
 Love: is promoted as the learner portrays respect in providing positive feedback to peers during practise of galloping

activity.

 Respect: is enhanced as the learner allows other chances while demonstrating galloping skills.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion: is fostered as the learner embraces own and others performance during practise of galloping.

Link to other subjects:

 Environmental activities: as the learner learns about directions.

 Religious activities: as the learner learns positive values while providing feedback to peers.

Suggested learning resources:

Safe space or playground, digital devices, reference books, relevant virtual sites, assistive technology such as universal

cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such

as head wand
